What is SOC2 compliance, and why it is important?

SOC 2, or \*\*System and Organization Controls 2\*\*, is a widely recognized framework developed by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) for managing customer data based on five “trust service criteria”: \*\*security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy\*\*.

SOC 2 compliance means that an organization has implemented rigorous internal controls and processes to protect customer information in a way that meets strict industry standards. It is particularly relevant for cloud service providers, SaaS companies, and any business that handles sensitive customer data.
At Neostella, SOC 2 isn’t just a checkbox—it’s a cornerstone of how we approach data security and reliability. Here’s why it matters:
\- \*\*Data Protection\*\*: Ensures your data is safeguarded from unauthorized access or breaches.
\- \*\*Operational Excellence\*\*: Demonstrates that systems are available, accurate, and reliable.
\- \*\*Trust & Transparency\*\*: Builds confidence with customers, partners, and auditors through third-party attestation.
\- \*\*Competitive Advantage\*\*: Sets your organization apart by showing commitment to security best practices.

citations.title: neostella opens partner ecosystem for case management platform. - Neostella
excerpts: At ILTACON today, Neostella showcased its [**Neostella Partner Program**](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fneostella.com%2Fpartnerships%2F&esheet=54593950&newsitemid=20260824676948&lan=en-US&anchor=Neostella+Partner+Program&index=1&md5=d5b97704fe3b0e7e95e8dd09ea6b4e90) , inviting technology vendors and service providers across categories to build, integrate and grow within its open ecosystem. The program expands Neostella’s approach to legal technology: giving firms the flexibility to choose the tools that work best for their business without forcing them into a closed technology environment.

Legal teams rely on more technology than ever to manage cases, communicate with clients, automate work and run their firms. But as technology stacks expand, another challenge has emerged: disconnected systems that create fragmented data, workflows and processes across the firm. According to Consilio’s 2026 Global Survey, 41% of legal professionals say fragmented tools that do not integrate well are their primary systems issue.

Built as the first fully open-API, enterprise-grade legal case management platform, Neostella was designed to connect and not control the technology firms use. Its API-first architecture allows legal teams to bring together the systems they already rely on while connecting data and workflows across their operation.

“Law firms shouldn’t have to choose between the technology they want and the ability to have those technologies work together,” said Scott Bickley, Vice President of Partnerships at Neostella. “Our partner strategy is built around giving firms more choice. We want technology providers to be able to connect, build and innovate within our ecosystem, while giving firms the flexibility to create the technology environment that works best for their business.”

With Neostella, firms can run more of their operations directly on the platform or continue using specialized solutions that work for their business – including billing and accounting, calendars and communications, AI-powered case review, client intake, court e-filing and more.
**Integrate or consolidate, it’s their choice.**

Neostella serves as the connected foundation beneath it all, keeping data and workflows together even as work moves across different applications. As new technologies emerge and business needs change, firms can connect, replace or add tools without rebuilding their technology infrastructure around a single vendor or trapping their data within one ecosystem.
The **Neostella Partner Program** extends that same flexibility to partners, offering several ways to participate based on their technology, services and business model:
* **Application Partners** can build integrations with the Neostella platform using its open API, real-time webhooks and Kafka event streams.

basis.reasoning: Neostella’s dated August 24, 2026 announcement says it opened the Partner Program, inviting technology providers to build and integrate within an open ecosystem for its case-management platform; this is a major platform/ecosystem launch within the six-month window.
